about: Differences that are listed and explained rather than fixed (PLAN P7: a human reviews the differences, and the differences are listed). `rows` explains a report row whose status is `differs`, naming exactly the layers it differs in (`pixels`, `dom`, `meaning`, `behaviour`), so a difference on another layer still fails; `general` lists differences no single row shows. A failed row is never a residual.

general.why: P7 compares screenshots taken in Chromium 141 (Playwright 1.56.1, build 1194). The product ships in Electronite v37, whose Chromium is 138, so the comparison engine is not the shipped one. G2 adds one capture run of the Rust app inside Electronite, compared with the Chromium 141 run of the same build (Q-28).

The machine fingerprint lists every font face and its version, so a font added, removed or upgraded stops pixel comparisons until both sides are captured again on one machine. A fontconfig rule that changes which face draws a fallback glyph without changing the list is not caught.

The project chip's initials take each word's first character. tC4's `w[0]` takes the first UTF-16 unit, so a word that starts outside the Basic Multilingual Plane (a mathematical letter, many CJK extension characters) gives half of a surrogate pair, a broken glyph; the rebuild gives the whole character (`tc_ui::app::shell::project_initials`, test `astral_initial_is_whole`). Every other name gives tC4's initials, JavaScript's `\s` and full upper-casing included.

tC4 composes the Feedback attachment in the page at once, so its Send never waits. The rebuild's server composes it (`feedback/compose`, A5 D8), and Send stays off until the attachment is shown, so nothing is sent that the dialog did not show (`tc_ui::app::feedback::can_send`). A compose that fails says so in the attachment box in the shown language (`feedback.attachmentFailed`), and opening the report again keeps the typed text and composes again (journey `a compose that fails keeps Send off and says so; the next opening keeps the text and composes again`; test `a_kept_report_whose_compose_failed_composes_again_with_its_text`). No baseline screen shows it: tC4 has no compose to wait for or to fail.
